t: Parameswara, a Sumatran prince who had left Palembang and then Temasek, founded the city at a fishing village at the mouth of the Malacca River, and Ming China's protection kept Siam and Majapahit from conquering it.

The Portuguese took it in 1511 and built the fortress A Famosa, the Dutch took it from them in 1641 with the help of Johor, and in 1824 the British and Dutch agreed that it would pass to Britain, which handed over in 1825.
Under the British it was part of the Straits Settlements, the Japanese occupied it from 1942 to 1945, and Malaya became independent on 31 August 1957.
dyk: According to legend, Parameswara named the city after the tree under which he was resting when he saw a tiny mouse deer kick his follower's hunting dogs into a river.
ev: Parameswara announces that the place will be called Malaka
The first official Chinese trade envoy, Admiral Yin Qing, arrives
Zheng He brings a stone tablet and an imperial order raising the port to a country
The Portuguese under Afonso de Albuquerque capture the city
The Dutch East India Company, with Johor, take Malacca from the Portuguese
An Anglo-Dutch treaty places Malacca in British hands, and it is handed over in 1825
Japanese forces enter the city and occupy it until 1945

f.founded: Founded by Parameswara, a Sumatran prince; 1396 is the year in which he announced the name Malaka, after a legend of a mouse deer and a tree.
f.where: On both sides of the Malacca River near its mouth on the Strait of Malacca, on the south-western coast of the Malay Peninsula, in Malaysia, about 152 km from Kuala Lumpur.
f.known: The Malacca Sultanate and its entrepôt; ties with Ming China and Zheng He; conquest by the Portuguese in 1511; the fortress A Famosa; the Dutch capture of 1641; the Straits Settlements; the Peranakan, Chitty and Kristang communities
f.today: Malacca City is the capital of the Malaysian state of Malacca, and its historic core, with George Town, was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2008.
